00399 /**
00400  * @brief               Change the widget focus order for a window
00401  *
00402  * HxWindowSetFocusArray allows the application to change the focus order of
00403  * the widgets contained within a window.  This function should be called
00404  * before calling HxWindowEventLoop.
00405  *
00406  * By default, the focus order of widgets is by order of creation.
00407  *
00408  * The ID array should normally contain all of the widget ID's in the window.
00409  * If an invalid ID is passed into the array, no error is returned, but any
00410  * missing widgets will no longer be capable of receiving focus for purposes
00411  * of keyboard navigation.
00412  *
00413  * Passing an idCount of 0 disables the toolkit's handling of keyboard
00414  * navigation for the window.  If idCount is 0, then pIdArray can be NULL.
00415  *
00416  * If widgets are allocated after this function is called, the new widgets
00417  * are appended to the focus array.
00418  *
00419  * @param pWindow       IN:     Pointer to a window (or NULL for app window)
00420  * @param pIdArray      IN:     Array of widget ID's
00421  * @param idCount       IN:     Size of the widget ID array
00422  *
00423  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00424  *
00425  **/
00426 HxResult HxWindowSetFocusArray(HxWindow_t* pWindow, const uint32_t* pIdArray,
00427                                 int32_t idCount);
00428

00449 /**
00450  * @brief               Enter the main event loop
00451  *
00452  * HxWindowEventLoop is called by the application after the application set-up
00453  * is complete, and the application is ready to process input events.
00454  *
00455  * The timeout argument is used by the system to determine how long to
00456  * remain in the event loop.  After that many milliseconds, the event loop
00457  * will end as soon as there are no pending input events.
00458  *
00459  * The application's thread blocks until the next event occurs, or until the
00460  * timeout occurs.  A timeout value of 0 waits forever for events.  If the
00461  * timeout triggers, HX_TIMEOUT is returned.  HX_INTERRUPTED is returned if
00462  * the blocking action is interrupted due to a threading error.
00463  *
00464  * @param pWindow       IN:     Pointer to a window, or NULL for AppWindow
00465  * @param timeout       IN:     Timeout value, or 0 for no timeout
00466  *
00467  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if event loop exited by a call
00468  *                              to HxWindowExitEventLoop.
00469  *                              Returns HX_TIMEOUT if timeout triggers.
00470  *                              Returns HX_DESTROYED if pWindow is closed.
00471  *
00472  **/
00473 HxResult HxWindowEventLoop(HxWindow_t* pWindow, int32_t timeout);
00474

00568 /**
00569  * @brief               Set a window input event handler
00570  *
00571  * HxWindowSetHandler is available to applications that need to customize the
00572  * processing of input events for a window.
00573  *
00574  * Applications that override the default handler should save the default
00575  * handler before replacing it with a custom handler, and restore it when 
00576  * appropriate.  The application's handler should call the default handler
00577  * before exiting to ensure that system behavior (i.e., focus navigation 
00578  * using the tab key, detection of double and triple button click, scroll 
00579  * wheel acceleration) is preserved.
00580  *
00581  * If the custom key and mouse button handler returns HX_OK, the system then
00582  * calls the widget's key and mouse button callbacks.  If the application does 
00583  * not want the widget callbacks called, the custom handler must return
00584  * HX_EVENT_HANDLED.
00585  *
00586  * If pCallback is NULL, the default callback and data is restored.
00587  * hOldCallback and hOldData are ignored if set to NULL.
00588  *
00589  * Warning:  menus and drop-down boxes use mouse button handlers.
00590  * Applications should not replace their handlers while they are open.
00591  *
00592  * @param pWindow       IN:     Pointer to window, or NULL for AppWindow
00593  * @param selector      IN:     Selector for type of event handler
00594  * @param pCallback     IN:     Pointer to the new HxWindowEventFunc, or NULL
00595  * @param pData         IN:     User data, or NULL
00596  * @param hOldCallback OUT:     Handle to the old callback, or NULL
00597  * @param hOldData     OUT:     Handle to the old user data, or NULL
00598  *
00599  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK on success.
00600  *
00601  **/
00602 HxResult HxWindowSetHandler(HxWindow_t* pWindow, HxHandlerSelector_t selector,
00603                         HxWindowEventFunc pCallback, void* pData,
00604                         HxWindowEventFunc* hOldCallback, void** hOldData);

00606 /**
00607  * @brief               Get a window input event handler
00608  *

00659  * queue that repeat the event passed in as pEvent. For example, passing a key
00660  * down event would flush out repeat events for the same key, but not for other
00661  * keys.  This is used at the end of an event handler to avoid having an overflow
00662  * of input events when your handler may not finish before another event arrives.

00665  *                              what to flush from the queue.

00670 /**
00671  * @brief               Set receiver for scroll events
00672  *
00673  * HxWindowGrabScrollEvents specifies a widget that should receive all scroll
00674  * wheel and up/down arrow key events sent to the window, regardless of which
00675  * widget has focus.
00676  *
00677  * This API is typically used by dialogs that contains a dominant list and
00678  * several command buttons (like the file dialogs).  By sending all scroll
00679  * events to the list, the user can easily scroll through the list without
00680  * having to navigate to it.
00681  *
00682  * Only one widget can grab scroll events.  If this function is called more
00683  * than once for the same window, the last widget grabs the events.
00684  *
00685  * If pWidget is set to NULL, then no widget grabs the events for the window.
00686  *
00687  * If the grabbing widget is disabled or set invisible, then scroll events
00688  * are handled normally.
00689  *
00690  * The implementation of tab widgets (see hxtabs.h) hides and shows containers
00691  * in response to the user selecting the tab buttons.  If the container has a
00692  * child list that grabs scroll events, the application should listen for the
00693  * kHxTabsSelected message so that the list can release or grab scroll events
00694  * as its parent container is shown or hidden.
00695  *
00696  * @param pWindow       IN:     Pointer to a window, or NULL for AppWindow
00697  * @param pWidget       IN:     Pointer to widget, or NULL
00698  *
00699  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00700  *
00701  **/
00702 HxResult HxWindowGrabScrollEvents(HxWindow_t* pWindow, HxWidget_t* pWidget);

00720 /**
00721  * @brief               Lock the display, and get a pointer to its data
00722  *
00723  * HxWindowLockSurface is the accessor to the data pointer for the frame buffer
00724  * associated with a window.
00725  *
00726  * In order to get the pointer to the frame buffer, the frame buffer must be
00727  * locked down.  This prevents other threads from trying to draw to the frame
00728  * buffer at the same time.  While holding this lock, no other drawing can
00729  * occur.  Any attempt to draw will not cause an error, but the new data will
00730  * be ignored and not transferred to the display, even when the surface is
00731  * later unlocked.
00732  *
00733  * Consequently, the application must be very careful when using this API.
00734  * Every call to HxWindowLockSurface must have a matching call to
00735  * HxWindowUnlockSurface.  And care must be taken during the locked phase: the
00736  * application should not allow the event loop to run, which could cause a
00737  * screen update to get lost.
00738  *
00739  * In addtion to a pointer to the frame buffer, this function returns the
00740  * pitch, or bytes per row, of the frame buffer if pPitch is not NULL.
00741  *
00742  * @param pWindow       IN:     Pointer to a window, or NULL for AppWindow
00743  * @param hDstBuf       OUT:    Handle to the window's frame buffer
00744  * @param pPitch        OUT:    Pointer to the frame buffer pitch, or NULL
00745  *
00746  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK on success.
00747  *
00748  **/
00749 HxResult HxWindowLockSurface(HxWindow_t* pWindow, void** hDstBuf,
00750                                 int32_t* pPitch);
00751

00757  * to HxWindowLockSurface.

00760  *
00761  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK on success.
00762  *

00764 HxResult HxWindowUnlockSurface(HxWindow_t* pWindow);
